sections.skill: Strategy: list what each clue leaves
sections.relationship: Students decide "enough" by feel. Listing every possibility each clue leaves makes the decision exact: one possibility left means enough.
sections.author_note: Students decide "enough" by feel. Listing every possibility each clue leaves makes the decision exact: one possibility left means enough.

lesson.title: List what each clue leaves
text: List every possibility allowed before any clue.
Cross out the ones a clue rules out. If exactly one answer remains, the clue is enough.
Do this for each clue alone, then for the clues together.

example.title: Worked example (a different question)
prompt: n is a whole number from 1 to 10. What is n? Clue (1): n is odd. Clue (2): n is a multiple of 3.
steps: Clue (1) leaves 1, 3, 5, 7, 9: not enough. Clue (2) leaves 3, 6, 9: not enough.
Together: 3 and 9. Still not enough: a third clue is needed.
